title: Grateful Dead Live at Shrine Auditorium on 1968-08-23
lineage: 8 track multitrack Reels> Sonic Wizardry > DAT > Cassette > DATs > CDRs > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent multi‑track soundboard capture of a 1968 show featuring an all‑out Alligator‑Caution jam, soaring Dark Star and The Eleven, with crisp guitar tone and solid rhythm section despite occasional mud and track mismatches.
ai_review.review: The recording is a multi‑track SBD that generally sounds clear and vibrant, though listeners note occasional muddiness and a few glitches where the two tape sources meet. Musically the show is hailed as one of ’68’s finest – highlighted by an epic Alligator > Caution sequence, powerful Dark Star, The Eleven, Cryptical/Other One and a fiery St. Stephen, with Jerry’s guitar tone, Phil’s bass work and the drums praised throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly positive (average ★4.4), most praising both performance and sound quality; only a few low‑star outliers mention minor issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multi‑track SBD, generally crisp and detailed. Some reviewers report muddy sections, occasional drop‑outs and a noticeable shift when the two tape sources (first set vs. filler) splice together; mislabeling of tracks also noted.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A high‑energy, improvisational flow that moves from the bouncy Alligator jam into an extended Caution, then launches into a soaring Dark Star and The Eleven before winding down with Death Don't Have No Mercy. The show feels cohesive despite the two‑tape source issue.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his beautiful guitar tone after abandoning the Les Paul, tender solos, and leading epic Dark Star and vocal work on Death Don't Have No Mercy.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as amazing; solid bass foundation and “copilot” to Jerry’s leads.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ work highlighted as great (pre‑TC era), especially Pigpen’s bluesy organ passages.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill and Mickey lauded for perfect, tapestry‑weaving percussion throughout the set.
